clue.text: Not eating a little butter? Well remembered

parts.note: someone off their food is not eating
a pat is a small slab of butter

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a period of skipping even a scrap of butter on their toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known by heart and ready to recite is learned perfectly, memorised to the letter.

clue.text: Playing well in this class

definitions.meaning: a sportsperson playing well is said to be in good shape, on top of their game
a school year group, as in the sixth of these

explanation.surface: A teacher remarks on someone performing nicely in this lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top of one's game is called being in this; it is also a British school year group.

clue.text: No longer apprehensive of grammatical term

parts.note: what is no longer is over and gone
an apprehensive person is nervous, on edge

explanation.surface: Someone has stopped being nervous of some piece of grammar jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the verb form grammarians use for events that already happened, such as 'walked'.

clue.text: Attempts to include old people in party

indicators.note: the word for attempts is made to hold the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: attempts are tries

explanation.surface: A recruitment drive tries to bring older folk into a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Britain's Conservative Party are commonly called by this nickname.

clue.text: Source of petroleum as strand is developed

indicators.note: being developed suggests the letters of 'as strand' are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An oil-industry note: petroleum comes as a strand of resource is exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Bituminous sand deposits, as in Alberta, are mined and processed to extract crude oil.

clue.text: Press articles on country arresting a small number

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the pair of articles holds the number between them

parts.note: two definite articles, each 'the'
four is a small number
a state is a country

explanation.surface: Newspaper stories about a nation detaining a handful of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'articles' supplies the word twice, and 'arresting' holds the number between the two copies; 'on' means the articles come before the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalism collectively is traditionally called this, a power alongside the three estates of the realm.

clue.text: Dragon is ridiculously slow, for one

indicators.note: something done ridiculously is done absurdly, so the letters of 'Dragon is' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fire-breathing beast is said to be absurdly sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Slow' is an example of a traffic instruction painted or posted beside a road.

clue.text: A home key

parts.note: a flat is a home, an apartment

explanation.surface: A house key, the kind everyone carries.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a musical key, one semitone below A natural.

clue.text: Destitute person's way of escape from top floor?

definitions.meaning: a homeless, penniless person; the 's stands for 'is'

definitions.text: way of escape from top floor?
definitions.meaning: to get out from upstairs you go first downstairs and then outside

explanation.surface: A penniless person's only way out of a high attic.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant with no money or home is described by this hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: In advance, dish out jam

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before, in advance
to serve food is to dish it out

explanation.surface: A host plates up jam before the guests arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit jam is a sweet spread also called by this name, as in strawberry ones.

clue.text: Permits expressions of pain, after all

indicators.note: after says the cries of pain are placed following the word all

parts.note: 'ow' is a cry of pain, so several are OWS

explanation.surface: Someone lets out cries of pain once everything is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to let it happen, giving leave or consent.

clue.text: Mickey captivated by this play?

parts.note: Mickey Mouse would be caught in a spring-loaded rodent catcher, which is also the name of Agatha Christie's long-running stage whodunnit

explanation.surface: Was Mickey enthralled by watching this theatre show?
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's murder mystery has run in London's West End since 1952; the title names a rodent catcher.

clue.text: Holiday vessel said to belong to its staff

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is spoken and the matching sound is what goes in

parts.note: a vessel that belongs to its staff is the crew's own ship

explanation.surface: A rumour that the liner is owned by the people working on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger liner used for leisure voyages calling at several ports.

clue.text: Refuse to disallow capturing rook

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so the word for disallow holds the chess piece

parts.note: to ban is to disallow
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player declines to forbid the taking of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Husks separated from grain are discarded as waste, chaff or rubbish.

clue.text: A wearing sort of business

parts.note: wearing looks like tiring but means to do with clothes worn: the clothing industry

explanation.surface: Someone complains of an exhausting job.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the informal name for the clothing and fashion industry.

clue.text: Folk hero is to steal, wearing mask

parts.note: to rob is to steal
in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'
a hood covers and hides the face

explanation.surface: A legendary figure is out to steal while wearing a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw of Sherwood Forest who robbed the rich for the poor is an English legend.

clue.text: Bishop once said to be struggling

indicators.note: struggling words are in difficulty, so 'once said' is jumbled

explanation.surface: A churchman was once reported to be having a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop presiding over a diocese is so called, the noun form of the adjective.

clue.text: Venomous six of the Romans die

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A grim tale: half a dozen Romans die by poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake-like and spiteful, poisonous in nature or speech.

clue.text: Roughly losing head in a fight

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for roughly drops its first letter

parts.note: about means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: A brawler gets knocked about and loses their head in a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing contest or spell of combat is called this.

clue.text: Spied moving towards lake, scatter

indicators.note: towards puts the lake's letter at the end, the way the rest heads
letters that are moving shift about, so 'Spied' is rearranged

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone spotted heading to the water makes the crowd break up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns SPIED into DISPE, with L added.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel doubts or crowds is to drive them away in different directions.

clue.text: Concerned with part of the orchestra coming back

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the percussion is the section with drums and cymbals

explanation.surface: A note about the drum section returning to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation or echo is a sound rebounding, and a consequence is an effect returning on its cause.

clue.text: Well-matched piece of pure quality

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A harmonious pairing praised as a fine specimen of excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides evenly balanced are a fair match, level in strength.

clue.text: Only a stretch of water

definitions.meaning: a lake or pond, as in Windermere

explanation.definitionFit: A 'mere trifle' is just a trifle; a small lake is also so called in British place names.

clue.text: Calls loudly and turns to buy drinks?

definitions.meaning: in British and Australian pub slang, your round of drinks is your turn to pay

explanation.surface: Someone bellows and it is their round at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To yell is to call out loudly; in pub slang 'my shout' means my turn to buy the round.

clue.text: This school once was sanctioned

definitions.meaning: an ... school was a former British residential institution for young offenders
was officially authorised, given the go-ahead

explanation.surface: A former school was given official permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctioned means officially allowed; British approved schools for young offenders were abolished in 1969.

clue.text: Wealth from work uncle wasted at end of life

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: wasted letters are ruined and reshaped, so 'uncle' is jumbled
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fortune from a job, which an uncle squandered by the end of his days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' turns UNCLE into ULENC; 'end of life' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Great riches and luxurious living are another way of saying affluence.

clue.text: Women pine regularly for young men's embrace

indicators.note: the young men's embrace holds the picked letters inside them

parts.note: lads are young men

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of 'pine'

explanation.surface: Women long, now and then, to be hugged by young fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like a tree but is a verb of longing in the surface; 'regularly' takes its second and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite plural for women, as on a toilet-door sign or in 'ladies and gentlemen'.
